items.prompt: Explain how appropriate delegation can relieve Ulima’s purchasing bottleneck. Ulima Furniture requires the owner’s approval for every small replacement part, even though the workshop head knows the repair work. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Delegation gives a subordinate authority to make particular decisions while the manager keeps final responsibility. At Ulima every small part purchase waits for the owner, so the owner has become a decision bottleneck even though the workshop head understands the repair work. Authorising the head to buy parts up to an agreed spending limit lets repairs continue sooner and frees the owner for larger decisions. The owner should set the limit and review spending reports; removing the limit entirely would create a risk of overspending.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: Delegation gives a subordinate authority to make particular decisions while the manager keeps final responsibility.
Context: the owner approves every small part although the workshop head knows the repair work.
Effect: a spending limit lets repairs continue sooner and frees the owner, with oversight retained.

items.prompt: Draw a simple organisation chart showing Omano’s stated reporting relationships. Omano Supplies has an owner-manager. Production, sales and finance heads each report to the owner-manager. Workers A and B report to the production head; a sales assistant reports to the sales head; an accounts clerk reports to the finance head. [8]
items.canonical_answer:
To draw a simple organisation chart, identify the most senior position, group positions at the correct levels and join each subordinate to the position it reports to directly. Use role titles rather than a list of names without jobs. Do not connect neighbouring roles merely because they are at the same level: a connecting line would imply a reporting relationship not stated. Keep direct spans distinguishable from all lower-level staff. The chart makes formal authority visible and helps a new worker identify a supervisor, but it does not show the quality of management or the informal communication network. Check the finished chart against each reporting fact. A line accidentally bypassing a supervisor changes the structure even if all job titles are present. ![Omano Supplies reporting structure](diagrams/omano-reporting.png)

Place the owner-manager at the top, the three heads at the second level and their direct staff at the third. The owner-manager’s span is three; the production head’s span is two. There are three levels. The chain from Worker A to the owner-manager goes through the production head, not the sales head.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: To draw a simple organisation chart, identify the most senior position, group positions at the correct levels and join each subordinate to the position it reports to directly.

items.prompt: Explain why expansion may require Kawa to change its structure and what effects could follow. Kawa Packaging grows from five to twenty staff, but its owner still approves every order and work allocation. Customers are waiting for decisions. [6]
items.canonical_answer: A small owner can coordinate a few staff directly, but growth may increase the number, variety and location of decisions beyond that person’s capacity. Appointing functional managers can introduce specialist skills and clarify responsibility. Delegating routine decisions can let local staff respond sooner and free senior management for wider planning. These changes require competent staff, clear authority and communication. More levels may lengthen the formal chain, increasing delay or distortion; extra managers also cost money. Alternatively, flattening the structure may shorten communication while giving remaining managers wider spans. Expansion does not dictate one correct shape. A business with risky technical work may need closer supervision than one with experienced staff carrying out familiar tasks. Review whether the proposed changes solve the actual overload and whether control remains adequate. Appointing an operations head with authority over routine allocations can reduce delay and provide supervision. The owner should specify decision limits and reporting. Adding a manager without passing any authority would add cost while leaving the original bottleneck in place.
marking_guidance: Starting point: A small owner can coordinate a few staff directly, but growth may increase the number, variety and location of decisions beyond that person’s capacity.
Because: credit the specific case link or contrast stated in the answer; a copied name alone is insufficient.
Effect: credit the developed explanation or correctly executed working, rather than a repeated assertion.
Worker: credit the stated result/effect with its beneficiary or units, as applicable.

items.prompt:
Tuli Foods has expanded. The general manager currently approves routine work allocations and delays occur. The proposed chart puts the general manager above production, sales and finance heads. A production team reports to the production head, a sales assistant to the sales head and an accounts clerk to the finance head. The heads know their functional work well, but spending limits have not yet been agreed.

a(i) Define delegation. [2]
a(ii) State two structural changes that business expansion may require. [2]
b State the meaning of responsibility and the meaning of span of control. [2]
c Explain how Tuli’s proposed reporting structure could help it manage expansion. Include the proposed chart relationships in your explanation. [6]
d Evaluate delegating routine work-allocation decisions to the three heads. [8]
items.canonical_answer: a(i) Giving a subordinate authority for particular tasks while the delegating manager retains final responsibility. a(ii) Appointing specialist functional heads; adding a supervisory level so that each manager’s span of control stays manageable. b Responsibility is the duty to complete a task satisfactorily; span is the number of direct subordinates. c Put the general manager at the top and the three heads beneath, then each specified team or assistant directly below the appropriate head. This gives the general manager a direct span of three and clarifies functional supervision. Heads can coordinate their areas, reducing the general manager’s direct workload and giving staff a clear reporting route. An extra level can delay communication, so authority must be real rather than sending all routine decisions upward. d The heads’ functional knowledge supports delegation and their faster work allocations could reduce the stated delays. Against this, undefined spending limits could cause inconsistent or excessive commitments and the general manager remains accountable. Delegate routine allocations with clear boundaries and review arrangements; keep major commitments centrally approved. Adding titles without authority would leave the bottleneck, while unrestricted authority is not needed to solve it.

items.prompt:
Tuli Foods has expanded. The general manager currently approves routine work allocations and delays occur. The proposed chart puts the general manager above production, sales and finance heads. A production team reports to the production head, a sales assistant to the sales head and an accounts clerk to the finance head. The heads know their functional work well, but spending limits have not yet been agreed.

a Explain what Tuli’s proposed organisation chart would show and how it could improve accountability as the business expands. [8]
b Evaluate retaining central approval of all routine decisions compared with delegating within limits. [12]
items.canonical_answer:
a The chart puts the general manager above the three heads, with each team or assistant under its specified functional head. It has three levels and a direct general-manager span of three. Staff can identify the supervisor responsible for work and where to report problems; heads can be held answerable for their functional activities. The chart clarifies the formal chain and reduces uncertainty about who allocates work, but does not by itself grant discretion or prove effective cooperation. Actual authority and communication must match the boxes and lines.

![Tuli proposed structure](diagrams/tuli-reporting.png)

b Central approval can preserve consistency and allow senior oversight of substantial risk, but approving every routine allocation is already causing delays and leaves knowledgeable heads underused. Delegation can improve response and free the general manager for expansion planning. It also creates a need to specify limits, report performance and coordinate between functions. Delegate routine decisions to the experienced heads within agreed limits because that directly addresses the current bottleneck. Retain central decisions for major commitments and review outcomes. This is preferable to either unrestricted discretion or unchanged approval of every small matter; if competence or control proved inadequate, the delegated limits should be tightened.

items.prompt:
Nari Repairs has grown to twelve operational staff plus two supervisors. Two experienced supervisors report to the owner and six staff report to each supervisor. Routine work decisions still await the owner, causing delays. The supervisors can make competent routine decisions if authorised within clear limits. The owner is deciding whether to delegate these decisions.

Evaluate delegating routine decisions to Nari’s supervisors. Give an answer plan that explains the formal reporting structure. [12]
items.canonical_answer: Structure: owner above two supervisors, each above six staff; owner span two, supervisor span six. Delegation transfers task authority but not the owner’s final responsibility. Benefit: competent supervisors can decide routine matters sooner, relieving the stated delay and allowing the owner to focus on wider needs. Risk: inconsistent choices or poor coordination if boundaries and reporting are unclear. Judgement: delegate within agreed limits and monitor outcomes, because experienced supervisors are available and central approval is the bottleneck. Do not change the owner’s span by counting the twelve indirect reports. The choice depends on competence and control, not on decentralisation being universally superior.

items.prompt:
Nari Repairs has grown to twelve operational staff plus two supervisors. Two experienced supervisors report to the owner and six staff report to each supervisor. Routine work decisions still await the owner, causing delays. The supervisors can make competent routine decisions if authorised within clear limits. The owner is deciding whether to delegate these decisions. For part (b) only, both experienced supervisors leave and are replaced by newcomers with no supervisory experience. Other facts remain unchanged.

a Evaluate delegated routine decision authority in Nari’s original structure. Describe the chart’s reporting relationships as part of your answer. [12]
b Evaluate the same proposal after the supervisors are replaced by inexperienced newcomers. Explain whether the judgement changes. [12]
items.canonical_answer: a The owner has two direct supervisor reports; each supervisor has six direct staff. The three-level chart defines the chain but current decisions still await the owner. Delegation would let experienced supervisors allocate routine work faster while retaining the owner’s final responsibility. Clear limits and reporting reduce inconsistency, although the owner must still monitor the results. Delegate because the necessary competence is stated and the approval delay is a real constraint. The benefit comes from moving authority, not merely redrawing boxes. b The formal chart and direct spans remain unchanged, but the competence condition has changed. Broad immediate delegation now risks errors and insufficient support for six staff per newcomer. Keeping every decision with the owner would preserve the original delay, so use narrower authority with close checking initially, and develop competence before widening it. On these facts reduce the initial scope of delegation rather than abandoning it permanently. The original wide routine discretion is less justified because experienced judgement is no longer available.
